title: Ki Tisa: show me thy glory (Exodus 33:18–23)
hookLine: Moses asks to see God, and sees only from behind, from a cleft in the rock

cards: Between yesterday's verses and today's, the story has broken apart. While Moses was on the mountain, the people made a golden calf. Moses came down, saw them dancing, and broke the tablets of stone.

Then came the long climb back: pleading for the people, pitching a tent outside the camp, speaking with God face to face, the text says, as a man speaks to his friend. And now Moses asks for one more thing.

teach.b: In the JPS 1917 translation, it's one short line: "Show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory." God's answer comes in layers. First, a yes: I will make all My goodness pass before you, and call out My name.

teach.h: NO ONE SEES MY FACE AND LIVES.
teach.b: Then a no: you cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live. Then a way through. There's a place by Me, God says: stand on the rock.

teach.h: A CLEFT IN THE ROCK, A HAND.
teach.b: I'll put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand while I pass by. And then: "I will take away My hand, and thou shalt see My back; but My face shall not be seen."
So Moses, who spoke with God as a man speaks to his friend, sees only from behind. What does that mean? The Torah doesn't explain, and Jewish readers have taken it in different ways.
The Talmud, in Berakhot, says God showed Moses the knot of the tefillin at the back of the head: a picture, not a portrait.
Maimonides says the face means God's essence, which no mind can grasp, and the back means God's ways in the world, which can be learned.

And some readers hear something quieter: a person rarely sees God coming, only where God has been. Only looking back, at a hard year, a rescue, a meeting that changed everything, does someone sometimes say: there.

how: This passage, Exodus 33:12–34:26, is also the Torah reading for the Shabbat during Passover and Sukkot, so in some years Moses' request is heard again on those festivals.

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: Moses sees God's face on the mountain
God says no one can see My face and live. Moses sees only from behind.
this request comes after the golden calf
after the calf, the broken tablets, and Moses' pleading for the people.
the Torah explains what God's back means
it doesn't. the Talmud, Maimonides and others offer different readings.

games.q: you're Moses. you've just pleaded the people back from the golden calf. you have God's ear. what do you ask for?
o: to be released from leading them.
games.why: show me, I pray Thee, Thy glory. God puts him in a cleft of the rock, covers him with a hand, and lets him see only from behind.

practice: Think of a time that was hard while you were in it, and without reliving the worst, walk forward from there in your mind to now. Who showed up, what held, what turned out differently than you feared?
If you pray, say thank you for it; if not, just let yourself see it.
